evals.prompt: I want to plan a change so retention can differ per tenant instead of one global value. Interview me before you draft the plan. The code is in evals/files/retention/. Keep notes in notes/ so I can resume in a new session. Reply with your first message to me only.
evals.expected_output: States verified facts from the code (30 days, read in cleanup.py and report.py), then asks only human-only questions, each with a recommendation attached. No plan yet.
expectations: The reply states that retention_days is currently 30
The reply states that the value is read in both cleanup.py and report.py
The reply does not ask the user where retention is read or what the current value is
The reply asks at least one question only the user can answer, such as what a tenant without an override gets, or whether report.py should follow the per-tenant value
Every question carries the assistant's recommended answer or a proposal
The reply does not contain the implementation plan itself
notes/index.md exists, states the goal in a sentence and links the other notes files
The notes record the verified facts (30 days, read in cleanup.py and report.py) with their source files
The notes list the questions asked as open items marked blocking or parked
The notes contain no user answers that the user has not given

evals.prompt: Before we start, make sure we're aligned: I want to add notifications to my side-project habit tracker. There is no code yet. Keep notes in notes/ so I can resume in a new session. Reply with your first message to me only.
evals.expected_output: Asks scope and preference questions with proposals. Does not assert facts about a codebase or stack that does not exist.
expectations: The reply asks at least one question about intent or scope, such as channels, triggers or who receives them
Every question carries a recommended answer or a proposal
The reply does not state facts about an existing codebase, stack or framework as if verified
The reply does not contain a finished design
notes/index.md exists and states the goal in a sentence
The notes record the user's request verbatim
The notes contain no invented facts about a codebase or stack

evals.prompt: Rename retention_days to retention_period_days everywhere in evals/files/retention/. Reply with what you changed.
evals.expected_output: Near miss: the task is fully determinable, so it just does the rename with no interview.
expectations: All three files use retention_period_days and none still use retention_days
The reply asks the user no questions
